name: Bergen
description: Bergen is a domino game for 2–4 players using a standard double-6 set (28 tiles). Players extend a single line of dominoes from both ends, scoring points when the two open ends match — two points for a 'double header' (both ends same number), three points for a 'triple header' (both ends same number, one of which is a double tile). The first player to discard all tiles scores two additional points. First to reach 15 points (2-player) or 10 points (3–4 player) wins.

history.origins: The origins of Bergen are not definitively known. The name may reference the Norwegian city of Bergen or Bergen op Zoom in the Netherlands, but no confirmed historical connection has been established. It belongs to the broad family of line domino games, likely European in origin.
timeline: Pre-20th century: Game believed to be of European origin.
20th century: Documented in English-language domino rulebooks.
Present: Played as a family and recreational domino game worldwide.
history.cultural: Bergen is a straightforward domino game favoured for teaching domino fundamentals to new players due to its simple scoring principle.
history.evolution: Bergen's distinctive 'matching-ends' scoring system — awarding points for double headers and triple headers — sets it apart from pip-count scoring games like Muggins. The ability to play with larger domino sets (double-9, double-12) for more players was a later adaptation.

setup.players: Bergen is played by two to four players using a standard double-six set. With more than four players, two or more double-six sets can be combined. Each player's initial draw and boneyard size depend on the count: two players get six tiles each (boneyard 16), three get six each (boneyard 10), four get five each (boneyard 8). Two boneyard tiles are reserved and never drawn.
setup.deck: Standard double-6 domino set (28 tiles). For 5+ players, two double-6 sets can be combined.
setup.dealing: 2 players: each draws 6 tiles. 3–4 players: each draws 6 tiles. Remaining tiles form the boneyard (2 tiles reserved and never drawn as a convention). Player with the lowest double plays first.
setup.equipment: 28 dominoes (double-6 set). Chips or score sheet for tracking points.

rules.objective: Be the first player to reach 15 points (2-player) or 10 points (3–4 player).
rules.gameplay: Players take turns extending the line of dominoes from either end. Scoring occurs when the end values match. If a player cannot move, they draw from the boneyard (leaving two tiles). The first to empty their hand scores a bonus.
keyRules: Doubles are played crosswise but are NOT spinners — the line extends only from the two ends, not from the sides of the double.
Two tiles must always remain in the boneyard and cannot be drawn.
Score immediately when a double header or triple header is formed.
First player to reach target score (15 or 10) wins; the current hand is completed before checking the total.

strategy.basic: Play tiles that create double headers or triple headers for immediate points. Prioritise playing doubles to set up a triple header.
strategy.intermediate: Suit counting: each pip value appears on 8 tile-ends in a double-6 set. Once a double is played, half that suit's ends are taken up. Use this to predict whether a double header will hold or be broken. Hold doubles as long as possible to convert a double header into a triple header.
strategy.advanced: Blocking strategy: if you realise you cannot score easily, aim to block the game by managing which suits are available at the ends. A blocked game awards 2 points to the lightest hand — sometimes deliberately constrain the ends to force a block when you hold fewer tiles than opponents. Track what opponents have drawn (if any) to infer their tile composition.
tips: Doubles are the most powerful tiles — they are both required for triple headers and hard to play offensively by opponents.
Target the same pip value at both ends as soon as possible; a triple header (3 pts) beats two separate double headers (4 pts total) only if you can sustain it.
In a blocked game, the player with the fewest tiles scores 2 pts — factor this into late-game play when your hand is light.

variations.name: Double Bergen
variations.description: Played with a larger domino set (double-9 or double-12), for more players or longer sessions. The first double played is typically a spinner in this variant, allowing four directions of play.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant uses a larger set and spinner rules that would need a dedicated engine configuration rather than simple overrides.

variations.name: Going Domino Variant
variations.description: In some variants, going domino scores 5 points instead of 2, making hand-emptying strategy more central.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes the bonus for going domino; scoring is documented in rules text without wired engine overrides.

variations.name: Highest Double Leads
variations.description: In some regions, the player with the HIGHEST double (6-6) plays first instead of the lowest double (0-0).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This local rule only changes who leads the first round and is represented descriptively instead of engine overrides.

scoring.description: Double header (both ends match) = 2 pts. Triple header (both ends match, one is a double tile) = 3 pts. Going domino = 2 pts. Blocked game = 2 pts to lightest hand.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach 15 points (2-player) or 10 points (3–4 player).

synthesis.shortDescription: A classic domino scoring game where you earn points every time both ends of the line match the same number. Two points for a double header. Three for a triple header (when one end is a double tile itself). First to 15 wins.
